Build with agents

Start a task, guide the work, and review the result.

Choose your model

Open Settings → Agents → Models.

  • Codex or Claude Code: use Sign in to connect your account. If the CLI is missing or too old, copy the displayed install or upgrade command, run it in your terminal, then choose Check. ByteQuay does not install or update these CLIs itself.
  • Your agent API: choose Add API key, select a supported provider, such as DeepSeek, enter a label and key, then Add key. DeepSeek tasks require Codex CLI, but not a Codex account.
  • Once Ready, choose your Development and Review models. Use repository Model overrides for a different choice.

Keys are stored encrypted on your Mac. Saved OpenAI keys cannot run agent tasks yet. Installing a CLI or saving a key alone is not enough: the CLI must meet the required version, and the selected account or key must have an available model. Today and Assistant use the global Development selection; an account available only to one repository cannot enable them.

New agent actions stay hidden until the selected agent and model are usable. Existing tasks, reviews, and notices remain available.

Keep Claude Code accounts separate

Use multiple accounts with isolated sign-ins and sessions.

  1. In Models → Claude accounts, choose Add Claude account. Enter a name and email, then Add and sign in.
  2. Select the account for Development or Review. Global accounts are available across repositories.
  3. For a dedicated account, add it in the repository’s Model overrides, or choose Use only here on a global account. Other repositories cannot use it.

Changing defaults affects new tasks. Existing tasks keep their selected account.

Start an agent task

  1. Open Tasks → + New task and choose a ready model.
  2. Describe the outcome, useful context, and how to check success.
  3. Review Automation, then Send. ByteQuay prepares a separate branch and working copy.

Steer adds guidance when supported; Run next queues a message. Stop this turn interrupts the agent.

Review approvals, inspect WorkBench → Changes, and check tests before Mark it complete.

Check limits in Usage. Add reusable instructions in Settings → Agents → Skills.

Deliver changes and repair CI

Review Automation before starting:

  • Auto draft PR: pushes commits and creates or updates a PR.
  • Auto CI fix: repairs supported failures, reruns CI, and can mark a draft ready. It can write to GitHub. CI repair agent follows Development unless you choose another supported agent.
  • Auto review summary: adds private analysis and a suggested plan for new review comments on the task’s PR.
  • Auto draft review replies: analyzes new review comments and prepares private replies. Choose Use draft, edit the reply, then Comment to publish it. Generated replies are never posted automatically.
  • Keep commits local for this turn: skips publication and CI follow-up.

These automation options start off on a fresh installation; existing choices are preserved. Completed development work is committed automatically. Change defaults for new tasks during setup or in Settings → Agents → Workflow, and review each task’s choices before sending. Automatic analysis and repairs use your model allowance. Use Stop automation and continue… to resume development. You review and merge the PR.

Cherry-pick and backport

  1. In Commits → History, choose the destination and source.
  2. Select commits, then Cherry-pick. Check the plan with Dry run, then Start cherry-pick.
  3. Follow progress in Commits → Cherry pick.
  4. Review the result, then Deliver this generated branch → Push branch and Create pull request. PR creation also starts the disclosed CI monitor.

For chained backports, set Related workspaces in repository settings and choose Backport. Follow Tasks → Backport chains. Each step waits for its source PR to merge.
